players.name: Jens Lehmann
players.note: Germany’s first choice and an ever-present in an unbeaten side; elite, a rung below the very best keepers.

players.name: Thierry Henry
players.note: Anchor season (97). The jump from 85 in his first English campaign reflects four years of development: in 1999/00 he was a converted winger still learning the centre-forward role, not the finished article.

players.name: Kolo Touré
players.note: A converted midfielder who was an unbeaten side’s first-choice centre-back at 22; pace and recovery already elite.

players.name: Sol Campbell
players.note: Four seasons on and at his peak - the best centre-back in the division in the unbeaten season, and in the world conversation.

players.name: Robert Pirès
players.note: World class that season — fourteen goals and eight assists from the left in an unbeaten side.

players.name: Ashley Cole
players.note: The best left-back in the league at 22 and England’s first choice.

players.name: Lauren
players.note: A dependable, athletic starter at right-back for the Invincibles; good rather than elite in his own right.

players.name: Gilberto Silva
players.note: An undemonstrative but excellent screening midfielder and a World Cup winner; a clear starter in an all-time great side.

players.name: Patrick Vieira
players.note: Captain of an unbeaten title side. Physically dominant and technically excellent — genuinely world class.

players.name: Freddie Ljungberg
players.note: Four seasons of development on from 1999/00: by the Invincibles year he was an elite wide forward, timing runs beyond the front line rather than holding the touchline.

players.name: Dennis Bergkamp
players.note: Thirty-four and rotated through the Invincibles season; still the best technician in the side.

players.name: Ray Parlour
players.note: Ten years on from the previous season here: a mature, England-capped midfielder rotating through the unbeaten Arsenal side.

players.name: Edu Gaspar
players.note: A rotation midfielder in an unbeaten side, but a Brazil international with genuine passing quality in his own right.

players.name: Pascal Cygan
players.note: Much mocked, but a competent squad centre-half in an unbeaten side who went on to win a league title in Spain.

players.name: Sylvain Wiltord
players.note: A France international and European champion used as a rotation forward at 29; still a quality top-four attacker rather than a squad filler.

players.name: Gaël Clichy
players.note: Eighteen, already quick and positionally sound enough for Wenger to use in a title season, but a long way from the France international he became.

players.name: José Antonio Reyes
players.note: Arrived in January at 19 for £17m and was immediately a difference-maker in short bursts; the ceiling is higher than the season, but the season is already good.

players.name: Martin Keown
players.note: Aged 37 and a fringe option by the Invincibles season.
